name: Creative Network Dynamics — DMN–Executive Coupling for Divergent and Convergent Processing
short_description: Creativity emerges from dynamic coupling between DMN (idea generation) and executive networks (idea evaluation); environments modulate coupling strength and phase switching
structural_pattern: Creative cognition requires dynamic coupling between three networks: (1) Default-Mode Network (medial PFC, posterior cingulate, angular gyrus) for generating novel associations; (2) Executive-Control Network (dorsolateral PFC, inferior frontal gyrus) for evaluating and selecting; (3) Salience Network (anterior insula, dorsal ACC) for orchestrating switches between generative and evaluative phases. The creative process involves temporal cycling: early GENERATIVE phase (DMN dominant, weak executive coupling) → salience-mediated TRANSITION (meta-awareness of promising idea) → EVALUATIVE phase (strong executive coupling). Environments modulate this coupling through sensory richness, which calibrates salience network switching rate.
higher_order_principle: Creativity is a network dynamic, not a brain region. The optimal creative state involves flexible alternation between generative (DMN-dominant) and evaluative (executive-dominant) phases. Environmental features that support this flexibility — moderate sensory richness, neither understimulating nor overstimulating — produce better creative output than environments that lock the brain into either extreme.

network_dynamics.dmn_role: Generates candidate ideas through spontaneous associative processes
network_dynamics.ecn_role: Evaluates and selects among candidates for originality and appropriateness
network_dynamics.salience_role: Orchestrates switching between generative and evaluative modes
network_dynamics.creative_coupling: High-creativity individuals show stronger DMN–ECN functional connectivity during divergent thinking

generative_phase.network_state: DMN dominant with weaker executive coupling
generative_phase.cognitive_mode: Associative flow with loose goal direction
generative_phase.environmental_support: Moderate noise (65-70 dB), high ceiling (R_h > 0.35), dim (100-200 lux)

transition.cognitive_event: Noticing that generated idea is worth evaluating

evaluative_phase.cognitive_mode: Screening candidates for novelty AND appropriateness
evaluative_phase.environmental_support: Quiet (<45 dBA), bright (400-500 lux), standard ceiling (R_h 0.25-0.35)

sensory_richness_optimum.description: Moderate sensory richness calibrates salience network switching at optimal rate
sensory_richness_optimum.understimulation_effect: Fails to engage salience network switching mechanism
sensory_richness_optimum.overstimulation_effect: Locks executive control into reactive mode, blocks generation
sensory_richness_optimum.goldilocks_prediction: Inverted-U for creative output as function of environmental complexity

coupling_flexibility.measure: Alpha power variability over prefrontal cortex
coupling_flexibility.high_creativity_marker: Higher alpha variability (more flexible DMN–ECN switching)
coupling_flexibility.environmental_modulation: Moderate complexity environments produce higher alpha variability

phase_appropriate_architecture.recommendation: Different environments for different creative phases

causal_links.evidence_base: Beaty et al. (2016, 2019); network connectivity studies establish the DMN–ECN coupling mechanism. Environmental modulation of coupling not yet directly measured.
Beaty et al. (2016): stronger DMN–ECN coupling predicts individual differences in creative ability (r ≈ 0.4).
Beaty et al. (2019): time-resolved connectivity shows phase dynamics within single creative trials. High-creativity = faster, more flexible cycling.

scope_conditions: Applies to individual creative cognition (collaborative creativity requires CREA4, future panel)
Domain-general mechanism — applies across verbal, visual, scientific, and artistic creativity
Most relevant for tasks requiring novel associations (divergent thinking, insight problems)
Does not model long-term creative development (plasticity effects)
moderators: Baseline creativity: high-creativity individuals may be less dependent on environmental support
Task phase: generative vs. evaluative phases have opposite environmental optima
Arousal level: moderate arousal supports flexible switching; high/low arousal impairs
Cognitive fatigue: fatigue reduces coupling flexibility; restoration (ART) is prerequisite

interactions.nature: CREA1 specifies a creative sub-state within T27's dynamic range. T27 describes the general DMN/TPN alternation; CREA1 specifies the creativity-specific coupling pattern.
Reactive control (T45) blocks creative coupling. Environments that trigger reactive control (high complexity, threat cues) impair creative network dynamics.
Attention restoration is a precondition for creative coupling. Fatigued attention impairs both DMN generation and executive evaluation.
CREA2 specifies the environmental channels that modulate CREA1's network dynamics.
CREA3 operates BETWEEN creative work episodes (incubation). CREA1 operates DURING active creative work.

key_references.citation: Beaty, R. E., Benedek, M., Silvia, P. J., & Schacter, D. L. (2016). Creative cognition and brain network dynamics. Trends in Cognitive Sciences, 20(2), 87–95.
Beaty, R. E., Seli, P., & Schacter, D. L. (2019). Network neuroscience of creative cognition. Current Opinion in Behavioral Sciences, 27, 22–30.
Christoff, K., Irving, Z. C., Fox, K. C. R., Spreng, R. N., & Andrews-Hanna, J. R. (2016). Mind-wandering as spontaneous thought: A dynamic framework. Nature Reviews Neuroscience, 17(11), 718–731.
Benedek, M., & Fink, A. (2019). Toward a neurocognitive framework of creative cognition. Current Opinion in Behavioral Sciences, 27, 116–122.
